newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends flat after CB action.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends flat after CB action.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended unchanged on Thursday after initial selling on the closure of the Central Bank's overnight borrowing facility was cancelled out by the unit's recovery on the offering of five-day reverse repos.
"It depreciated slightly this morning because of the overnight," said a trader. But as the dollar gained against peso, "people took profits," he added.
The focus on Friday will be on the overnight rate.
The Central Bank could cut its overnight borrowing rate to under the current 10 percent level, traders said.
If that happens, "we may see dollar at 26.35," a trader said. But he said it was possible the Central Bank would forestall such an action in order to prevent a drop in the peso.
Volume, although higher at $187.70 million from Wednesday's $118.90 million, was artificially swollen by the initial rush to sell the peso countered by a buying reversal, traders said.
"Volume usually averages 200 to 260," a trader said. "I think we will remain sideways until next week."
